source_caption:
The Boondocks follows brothers Huey and Riley Freeman, who move with their grandfather from Chicago to the mostly white suburb of Woodcrest. The brothers have very different personalities—Huey is politically aware and serious, while Riley is obsessed with hip-hop culture and street life.

In The Boondocks, the series uses sharp satire and dark comedy to tackle race, politics, class, pop culture, and social issues. Created by Aaron McGruder, the series features the voices of Regina King, John Witherspoon, and Gary Anthony Williams.

source_details.title: The Boondocks
source_details.synopsis: The Boondocks is an American adult animated sitcom created by Aaron McGruder for Cartoon Network's late-night programming block Adult Swim, based on his manga-influenced comic strip of the same name. The series focuses on a Black American family, the Freemans, and their experiences in the fictional, predominantly white suburb of Woodcrest. The perspective offered by this mixture of cultures, lifestyles, social classes, stereotypes, viewpoints and racialized identities provides for much of the series' satire, comedy, and conflict.
